summary: Sustained 5xx elevation from asymmetric upstream restart and HTTP/2 stream-slot starvation during mixed embed/chat burst
description:
Issue summary: Customers started seeing a sustained elevation in 5xx responses for streaming and short-chat requests beginning 2026-03-12 10:50 UTC. Errors primarily reported as 502/503 from the API gateway with 'upstream reset' and 'stream slot unavailable' symptoms.

Impact: NovaDocs (dedicated tenant) observed 30-45% error rate on streaming chat routes for ~2 hours, causing real user failures and increased retry traffic. Other tenants on the same pool experienced degraded tail latency.

Environment: prod/us-east, Dedicated GPU pool (reserved), hybrid streaming+embedding workload (mix ratio ~60/40).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a burst of concurrent streaming chat sessions (50-80 concurrent streams) mixed with medium-size embedding uploads (batch size ~128).
2) Observe API gateway returning intermittent 502/503 and aborts within 30s.
3) Checking runtime shows frequent short-lived restarts on a subset of replicas and many HTTP/2 streams stuck in HALF-CLOSED_LOCAL state.

Observed logs/snippets:
- apigw: "upstream reset before response completed" / "502 upstream connection reset"
- runtime: "runtime: panic at kv_prefetch.go:482" followed by fast restart and subsequent "http2: stream slot unavailable" warnings
- autoscaler: flurry of scale-up/scale-down events within 10m window (oscillation)

Customer notes: NovaDocs reported that failures aligned with a product campaign spike and asked for priority remediation and mitigation while we investigate.

Urgency: Customer-facing impact for a paying dedicated tenant during business hours. Escalated to SRE oncall.
comments: 2026-03-12 11:05 - NovaDocs (CS contact): 'We're seeing 50% of chat requests fail with 502s since ~10:50 UTC. Can you route us to another pool? This is blocking our customers.'
2026-03-12 11:12 - Support (Aisha Khan): Acknowledged. We're investigating and will provide mitigation steps within 15 minutes. Asked for tenant id and example request IDs.

2026-03-12 11:28 - SRE (Jonah Park): Early telemetry shows a localized restart pattern on 3/12 runtime replicas and HTTP/2 stream slot exhaustion. Temporarily routed NovaDocs to a warmed fallback pool and disabled hedged retries for their tenant. Error rate dropped to ~8% after routing change.
2026-03-12 12:10 - Support (Aisha Khan): Customer confirmed partial recovery after routing. They still see intermittent 503s on long-lived streams.

2026-03-12 13:40 - SRE (Jonah Park): Collected core dumps and runtime logs from affected replicas. Uploaded artifacts to internal S3: s3://redwood-incident/SUP-277338/ and created trace links. Hypothesis added to investigation notes.

2026-03-13 09:15 - Engineering (Priya Desai): Reproduced stream-slot leak locally with a mixed workload harness. Found a race in prefetch cancellation that prevented HTTP/2 stream closure on restart. Draft patch PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2314
2026-03-14 08:30 - SRE (Jonah Park): Patch approved for canary rollout. Plan: deploy patch to 10% of pool, monitor stream slot metrics and 5xx rate for 30m before wider rollout.
investigation_notes:
Timeline of actions and findings:
- 10:50 UTC: Error elevation begins correlated with NovaDocs campaign spike.
- 11:00 UTC: API gateway shows high upstream reset rates and increased connection re-establishments.
- 11:12 UTC: SRE observed three runtime replicas restarting repeatedly; their restart cadence aligned with prefetch worker failures in logs.
- 11:30 UTC: Evidence of HTTP/2 stream slot saturation: large number of HALF-CLOSED_LOCAL streams around affected replicas, preventing new stream allocation.
- 11:40 UTC: Autoscaler reacted to perceived capacity shortage then backfilled; rapid scale events amplified the issue via transient cold starts.
Hypotheses considered:
H1: Runtime prefetch cancellation race causes panic and restart, leaving half-closed streams -> downstream apigw 502s (most likely).
H2: Autoscaler cooldown misconfiguration causing oscillation that amplifies transient restarts (contributor).
H3: Client retry amplification (hedged retries) increased concurrent open streams (contributor).
Evidence: core dumps show prefetch goroutine stack consistent with known race. Canary reproduction confirms leak under mixed streaming+embed load.
Temporary mitigations applied:
- Rerouted NovaDocs to warmed fallback pool which significantly reduced 5xx rate.
- Disabled hedged retries at the tenant-level for NovaDocs.
- Increased HTTP/2 max-concurrent-streams soft limit on the gateway for the pool to reduce immediate rejections.
Next steps: roll out runtime patch to fix prefetch cancellation, adjust autoscaler cooldowns to prevent oscillation, update hedged retry defaults and add tenant-level backoffs.
Monitoring: dashboards updated (grafana link: https://grafana.redwood/s/incident/SUP-277338), alert thresholds lowered for stream-slot utilization.
resolution:
Workaround implemented: NovaDocs routed to fallback pool and hedged retries disabled for the tenant; HTTP/2 soft limit temporarily increased.
Permanent fix: merged runtime patch to properly cancel prefetch and ensure stream closure (PR merged 2026-03-13). Canary rollout completed 2026-03-14 09:10 UTC with success (5xx down to baseline).
Follow-up actions assigned:
- Adjust autoscaler cooldown and add jitter to reduce oscillation (owner: infra-autoscale team).
- Add automated acceptance test in the mixed-workload harness to detect stream-slot leaks (owner: runtime QA).
- Update runbook with steps for tenant routing during asymmetric restarts and document hedged retry opt-outs for large embedding/chat mixes.
Customer communication: NovaDocs informed of mitigation and planned fixes. They requested postmortem and we agreed to provide within 3 business days.
